exposure: Index mode of birth (spontaneous vaginal, instrumental vaginal, elective/emergency caesarean birth)
Maternity care funding model (public vs private hospital)
outcome: Subsequent birth modes (second and third births)
Trends of index and subsequent modes of birth over time
Prediction of subsequent birth modes based on index birth
cohort: The study included 172,041 low-risk nulliparous women from New South Wales, Australia, who had their first birth between 2001 and 2011.
finding: Women giving birth in public hospitals had higher proportions of spontaneous vaginal births compared with those in private hospitals, where caesarean sections were more common.
mod_finding: Women with an index spontaneous vaginal birth had a very high probability (91.3%) of having subsequent vaginal births, with similar probabilities in both public (91.6%) and private (90.2%) maternity care funding models.
followup_time: The study analyzed subsequent births over a 16-year period (2001-2016) after the index birth.
